title: Direct Response Agencies That Make UGC-Style Ads for Meta
summary: Direct response agencies that make UGC-style ads: AI presenter and real creator options compared by who appears on camera, price and Meta ad rights.
body_markdown:
## Other providers: Voy Media, Brighter Click, inBeat, Billo, Pinprick and Admiral Media


### Voy Media: a direct response agency with a UGC studio


Voy Media says it focuses on direct response and customer acquisition in ecommerce, lead generation and mobile. Its[Creative Studio page](https://voymedia.com/services/creative-studio/) lists native UGC, at-home creator videos, studio production, photography and copywriting, next to full-service Facebook and Instagram ads with retargeting, custom audiences and dynamic product ads. Packages are based on total ad spend, optimizations and growth, and no figures are published. Choose it when you want one direct response team to make the UGC and buy the media, and ask how many UGC-style ads a package includes each month.


### Brighter Click: real creators on a known batch


Brighter Click's[UGC agency page](https://www.brighterclick.com/ugc-agency) lists edited UGC videos from real creators in 9:16 and 4:5, with unlimited usage rights and whitelisting setup. Its package is $4,500 for 12 edited videos from 4 creators, which works out to about $375 per video by simple division. Turnaround is 10 to 14 business days for that package, and Facebook ads are a separate service.


### inBeat: creator sourcing with whitelisted ads


inBeat's[UGC agency page](https://inbeat.agency/ugc-agency) describes sourcing creators for fit, writing hooks and scripts, and running whitelisted ads and Spark Ads through creator handles, with usage rights defined before production. Pricing is not published, so ask for a scoped quote.


### Billo: a creator platform with partnership ads


Billo's[homepage](https://billo.app/) lists 5,000+ vetted creators, partnership ads that run from creator handles, and an optional managed service. Its pricing is not published on the homepage. Choose it when you want repeat creators, and settle in writing who handles creator selection, editing and account permissions.


### Pinprick: AI UGC with fees tied to ad spend


Pinprick describes an AI UGC agency for DTC brands that scripts, casts, produces and delivers test-ready UGC-style ads, with human creative directors reviewing every frame. Its[pricing page](https://pinprick.io/pricing) says eligible brands, mainly those already spending meaningfully on ads, pay no per-ad fee. Production is an agreed percentage of ad spend, and that rate is not published. Its agency page also headlines ten UGC ads for $2,000, without listed conditions, so ask what that offer requires.


### Admiral Media: fixed AI UGC batches


Admiral Media sells creator-style video ads for apps and ecommerce brands, made with AI presenters and finished with human editing and quality review. Its[AI UGC page](https://admiral.media/ai-ugc-agency/) lists Starter at €10,000 for 20 ads of up to 15 seconds, Growth at €16,000 for 40 of up to 30 seconds, and Pro at €29,000 for 80 of up to 60 seconds. Its ideal clients invest US$50,000 or more a month in paid media, and campaign and budget management is agreed separately.


## Which route fits your ad: real person, AI presenter or both


Start with the claim. If the ad relies on a customer's experience, a real person gives the claim its credibility. Admiral describes its AI UGC as scripted advertising, so an AI presenter should never claim to have used the product or deliver a customer's experience as fact. If the ad explains a product or a common problem, an AI presenter can carry the explanation, and the script does most of the work.


If you need both, split the work. Use AI presenters for product explainers and use creator handles for testimonials that must come from a real person. Ask each provider to show where each format sits in the batch, so the testimonial cut does not get swapped for a scripted one.


Then check the label and the rights. Meta says it labels ads[created or significantly edited with its own generative AI features](https://about.fb.com/news/2025/02/gen-ai-transparency-metas-ads-products/) , and that it will detect ads made with third-party AI tools and show an "AI info" label. Its post does not say that detection is live yet. Get usage rights in writing as well: Pinprick lists unlimited paid usage rights, Brighter Click lists unlimited usage rights, and inBeat defines usage rights before production begins.


## Key takeaways


- Knowlify is our top pick for scripted UGC-style ads with AI presenters, at about 25 finished ads a week, but not with real creators.
- Use a real creator when the ad must show a real customer or run from a creator's handle, and get the handle permission in writing.
- Voy Media is the clearest direct response agency here, pairing a UGC studio with Facebook and Instagram media buying, and Brighter Click sells 12 edited creator videos for $4,500.
- Pinprick and Admiral Media price AI UGC differently: a percentage of ad spend for eligible brands, or fixed batches in euros.
- Confirm usage rights, scripting approvals and the AI label before you commit to any batch.


## FAQ


### Which direct response agency makes UGC-style ads?


Voy Media says it focuses on direct response and lists native UGC and at-home creators in its Creative Studio, next to Facebook and Instagram media buying. Brighter Click, inBeat and Billo sell creator-made UGC, and Knowlify makes UGC-style ads with AI presenters. Choose by whether the ad needs a real person on camera and whether you want media buying in the same contract.


### Are AI presenter UGC ads the same as real creator UGC?


No. Admiral Media says AI UGC is scripted advertising, not content submitted by a real customer. Real creator UGC can run from a creator's handle under Meta's partnership ads, and an AI presenter has no handle of its own. Choose by whether the ad needs a real person on camera.


### Which UGC agency publishes a price per video?


Brighter Click publishes $4,500 for 12 edited videos from 4 creators, which is about $375 per video by simple division. Admiral Media publishes batch prices in euros, such as €10,000 for 20 ads up to 15 seconds. Billo and inBeat publish no price, and Pinprick headlines ten ads for $2,000 with no listed conditions.


### Can Knowlify run ads from a creator's handle?


No. We do not supply real human creators or post from creator accounts, so partnership ads from a creator's handle are outside our service. If that format is central to your plan, compare creator platforms such as Billo or inBeat.


### What does Meta require for creator-handle ads?


Meta's partnership ads documentation describes ads that run from a creator's or partner's handle, and its help center has a page on partnership ad permissions. Get the permission terms in writing in the contract before production starts, including what happens if the creator withdraws.
